## NativeCodec interface

Source for the in-process value codec.

**Signature:**

```typescript
interface NativeCodec
```

## Remarks

`prelude` is automation-process JavaScript that declares exactly two top-level bindings, [NATIVE_DECODE_FUNCTION](./core.native_decode_function.md) and [NATIVE_ENCODE_FUNCTION](./core.native_encode_function.md)<!-- -->, both holding functions, and defines no other globals. Their contract:

- `decode(wire, plan, env)` returns native values: dates as `Date`<!-- -->, integer text as numbers, special double states as `NaN`<!-- -->, `±Infinity`<!-- -->, or `-0`<!-- -->, app-specific bridge forms where the plan calls for them, and the app's own object for a reference it can address ([NativeCodecEnvironment](./core.nativecodecenvironment.md)<!-- -->). - `encode(native, plan, env)` returns JSON-safe wire values: no raw `NaN`<!-- -->, `Infinity`<!-- -->, or `-0`<!-- -->, no `Date` objects, and no own properties holding `undefined`<!-- -->. Absent optional fields are omitted. An app object at a reference position becomes an identity reference; one whose resource is found within a container must come with the record it was read through (<!-- -->), which becomes its container. A record field's value a body hands over marked as one its property's evidence lets read as absent (<!-- -->) encodes as `null` at a nullable position when the app reports its object missing (-1728) as the codec reads the object's identity. - Each marker is an object whose only own property is a registry symbol, and is honoured only at the position it is made for. A marker anywhere else is not a record, so it fails by its plan, under `unknown` too. A string key of the same name is ordinary data. - `env` is `{ app, references }`<!-- -->. Without it, no reference converts. - Under a `passthrough` plan, both functions return their argument unchanged, without inspecting it. - Under a `none` plan, `encode` returns `null` whatever the native result was, and `decode` returns `undefined`<!-- -->. - When a value violates the plan, either function throws an object whose `name` is [NATIVE_CODEC_ERROR_NAME](./core.native_codec_error_name.md) and which also carries `direction`<!-- -->, `path`<!-- -->, and `message`<!-- -->. Examples are a fractional value at an integer position, or an integer outside the supported domain. - When the plan has a kind the codec cannot convert, or a reference of a form or to a resource it cannot convert, either function throws the same object with `unsupportedKind` set to that kind, whatever the value is. - When `decode` addresses the object a reference names and the app has no such object, it throws the same object with `missingResource` set to the reference's resource; when the reference names a position its container's collection does not reach, with `outOfRangeResource` set instead. - When the app fails while `encode` reads a record field's value (a reference's identifier), the app's error is let through with naming that field and its position.
